title: In 1980, a Volcano Blew Sideways at 300 Miles an Hour

scenes.text: In 1980, a volcano blew sideways at 300 miles an hour.
Mount St Helens, Washington. A magnitude 5.1 earthquake shook the bulging north face loose.
The biggest landslide in recorded history. It uncorked the volcano, and the blast came out sideways.
At 300 miles an hour it flattened 230 square miles of forest and killed 57 people.
The ash column hit 80,000 feet in 15 minutes. A city 250 miles away went dark at midday.
When the ash cleared, the mountain was 1,300 feet shorter.

description:
On May 18, 1980, a magnitude 5.1 earthquake triggered the largest landslide in recorded history on Mount St. Helens, Washington, and the volcano exploded sideways.
The lateral blast travelled at least 300 miles an hour, flattened about 230 square miles of forest and killed 57 people. The ash column reached about 80,000 feet in under 15 minutes and turned Spokane, 250 miles away, dark at midday. The summit lost 1,314 feet of height.
Where were you, or your parents, in May 1980? Comment below.
first_comment: A geologist named David Johnston was watching from a ridge six miles away. His last radio message was: Vancouver, Vancouver, this is it. Would you have stayed to watch?
